markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

**Starting point.** (1) Existing probes measure training-score separation, while selection uses macro validation HR@10. Better margins therefore require independent ranking validation. (2) Feedback favors recent, repeated, specific interests. This motivates recency ablations, but does not establish current purchase intent. (3) Architecture compatibility enables controlled comparisons. Missing diagnostic observations must remain missing rather than becoming apparently healthy zeros.

**Related work.** (1) The supplied [2026 transition-model study](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling) motivates an inexpensive pairwise history branch. Its results do not establish gains under this benchmark. (2) [Liu et al.](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748042) identify availability confounding in history shuffling. Perturbation effects consequently need carefully matched controls. (3) [Sampling analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.02263) cautions that sampled and catalog-wide rankings can disagree. Catalog diagnostics should supplement the pinned selection metric.

These insights suggest three directions: explicit recency modeling, controlled behavioral diagnostics, and evidence-grounded interpretation.

### Framework

| Component | Existing evidence | Gap and proposed response |
|---|---|---|
| Sequence representation | SASRec compatibility hooks | Add a simple pairwise residual |
| Reliance on history | Training margins | Compare recent and matched older deletions |
| Recommendation meaning | Qualitative feedback | Separate supported evidence from unknown prerequisites |
| Selection | Fixed sampled HR@10 | Preserve protocol and report category effects |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Recency-weighted pairwise residual | 4/7/4 | Originality: useful combination, established ingredients. Potential: cheap complementary evidence, possible redundancy. Difficulty: small branch, requires inference synchronization. |
| Last-item-preserving history dropout | 3/6/2 | Originality: targeted augmentation, familiar method. Potential: robustness, possible loss of useful evidence. Difficulty: simple masking, careful sequence compaction. |
| Popularity-matched rank diagnostics | 4/6/3 | Originality: focused controls, established statistics. Potential: interpretable failures, no guaranteed optimization benefit. Difficulty: modest sampling code, potentially costly catalog scoring. |

### Selected idea: recency-weighted pairwise residual

At 0% progress, prioritize a small, reversible extension. Combine SASRec scores with low-rank directed item-transition scores averaged over history using exponential positional decay. A learned, category-specific nonnegative coefficient starts near zero. Repeated interactions contribute repeatedly; this is a modeling hypothesis, not evidence of intent or compatibility.

```text
for each category and training prefix:
    contextual = SASRec(prefix)
    weights = normalized exponential recency weights
    history_vector = sum(weights * source_embedding(prefix))
    score(item) = contextual_score(item)
                  + softplus(gate) * history_vector · target_embedding(item)
    optimize baseline loss using the combined scores
```

Use identical splits, seeds, routing and training defaults. Retain all diagnostic interfaces, restore model mode, and return counts plus unavailable values for empty probes. Update the predictor writer with the residual branch. Compare baseline and residual using pinned macro validation HR@10 within the shared budget; treat deletion probes and twenty-user feedback as explanatory evidence only.

idea.description: Add a recency-weighted, low-rank directed item-transition residual to each category's SASRec model. Jointly train the combined score while retaining the original data routing and evaluation protocol.
idea.motivation: The supplied feedback suggests that broad historical similarity sometimes outweighs recent specific evidence. A simple transition branch offers a testable way to strengthen that evidence without assuming observable ownership, compatibility, purchase intent, or simulator traits.
idea.implementation_notes: Use separate source and target item embeddings of dimension 32, with padding excluded from the normalized history average. For valid position j in a prefix ending at t, use weight proportional to exp(-(t-j)/tau), initially fixing tau=5 to limit search. Initialize the learned scalar gate so softplus(gate)=0.01 and initialize both embedding tables with small nonzero random values. Compute every training position from its causal prefix only; a cumulative exponentially weighted recurrence avoids quadratic history aggregation. Keep the baseline loss, optimizer, and epoch environment default initially. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; save checkpoints and generated working/predict.py beneath the trial directory. The predictor writer must serialize architecture settings and recreate both branches. DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) remain callable. Composite scoring must pass through view.predict_score; document that item-embedding alignment describes only the inspected table. Return explicit missing values and sample counts for unsupported diagnostics, and restore the actual model's prior training mode. Do not use unavailable review fields or item categories. Any additional diagnostic GPU work counts against the shared search budget.
idea.pseudocode:
For each routed category:
  initialize baseline SASRec and rank-32 source/target embeddings
  initialize gate with softplus(gate)=0.01
  for each baseline training batch:
    compute causal SASRec features
    compute causal normalized exponentially weighted source histories
    score positives and negatives with SASRec plus gated transition dot products
    optimize the unchanged baseline loss on combined scores
  save model and generate a matching predictor
Compare the baseline and extension using the unchanged host validation protocol; select by equal-weight macro HR@10.

originality.positive: Combines an interpretable transition residual with the existing contextual model in a controlled, category-specific extension.
originality.negative: Recency weighting, low-rank transitions, and additive model combinations are established techniques.

future_potential.positive: Provides an inexpensive foundation for testing whether simple transition evidence complements contextual sequence representations.
future_potential.negative: The branch may duplicate SASRec behavior or amplify popular transitions; benchmark gains remain unmeasured.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires two small embedding tables, a causal weighted recurrence, and an additive scoring path.
code_difficulty.negative: Training-position causality, diagnostic composite scoring, checkpoint loading, and generated inference must remain consistent.

related_work.title: Do Sequential Recommendation Benchmarks Require Higher-Order Sequence Modelling?
contributions: The supplied search summary reports strong recency-weighted pairwise transition baselines, motivating a simple transition branch.
limitations: The reported datasets and evaluation protocols differ from this RecHarness task.
Does not establish that an additive SASRec residual improves the specified macro HR@10.

related_work.title: Liu et al., RecSys 2025: availability-aware history shuffling
contributions: The supplied summary identifies item availability as a confound in arbitrary sequence shuffling.
limitations: Edited-history sensitivity does not identify causal changes in user preferences.
Availability constraints do not remove every distribution shift caused by perturbation.

related_work.title: On the Bias of Offline Evaluation Methods for Recommender Systems
contributions: Analyzes limitations of sampled recommendation evaluation and motivates distinguishing sampled rankings from full-catalog behavior.
limitations: Does not justify replacing the task's pinned sampled HR@10 selection criterion.
Does not establish which proposed architecture will perform best on these four categories.
